entries.label_vi: Học tại nhà → cá nhân hoá tốc độ, lịch linh hoạt theo sở thích, tránh bắt nạt
entries.claim: Homeschooling allows teaching to be tailored to the needs of each child.
entries.because: A parent working with one or two children can identify weaknesses and give targeted practice at once, and the timetable can follow the child's interests.
entries.result: Faster progress in strong areas and fewer problems such as bullying.
entries.reuse_vi: Ưu điểm cho đề học tại nhà, giáo dục cá nhân hoá, trường tư.

entries.label_vi: Học tại nhà → thiếu giao tiếp xã hội: không biết hợp tác, xử lý xung đột, tiếp xúc quan điểm khác
entries.claim: Learning mostly at home limits children's social development.
entries.because: School is where children make friends, resolve disagreements and work in groups, and meet peers from different backgrounds; at home they may spend most days with adults and siblings.
entries.result: Confidence and teamwork may suffer later in life; clubs and online classes help but need time and organisation.
entries.reuse_vi: Nhược điểm cho đề học tại nhà, học online hoàn toàn.

entries.label_vi: Học tại nhà → thiếu chuyên môn và cơ sở vật chất (phòng thí nghiệm, sân thể thao)
entries.claim: Homeschooling cannot match the expertise and facilities that schools provide.
entries.because: Few parents can teach every subject to a high standard, and laboratories, sports grounds and specialist equipment are rarely available at home.
entries.result: Pupils may leave with gaps in their knowledge that are difficult to repair.
entries.reuse_vi: Nhược điểm cho đề học tại nhà, học online, trường quá nhỏ.

entries.label_vi: Dạy đa ngôn ngữ → giáo viên: soạn tài liệu nhiều ngôn ngữ, cần bằng ngoại ngữ cao, lớp trình độ lẫn lộn, thiếu người đủ chuẩn
entries.claim: Multilingual education places considerable demands on teachers.
entries.because: Staff must prepare materials in several languages, hold advanced language qualifications and adapt lessons for pupils at very different levels; qualified bilingual teachers are scarce.
entries.result: Heavy workloads and weaker lessons unless training, assistants and shared materials are provided.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề song ngữ / đa ngôn ngữ, giáo viên thiếu và quá tải.

entries.label_vi: Đánh giá wellbeing → học tốt hơn, phát hiện sớm vấn đề; cả trường cải thiện chính sách; nhưng phải kín đáo
entries.claim: Wellbeing and learning are closely linked.
entries.because: Anxious, lonely or exhausted pupils concentrate less and fall behind; short surveys and conversations help schools identify problems early.
entries.result: Early help and policies on homework, bullying and pastoral support improve.
entries.rebuttal: Formal mood tests could stigmatise pupils, so use anonymous surveys, observation and counsellors, and keep data confidential.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề wellbeing học sinh, tư vấn học đường, áp lực học tập.

entries.label_vi: Điện thoại trong lớp → mất tập trung (được thiết kế để cạnh tranh sự chú ý); cấm là cách đơn giản bảo vệ giờ học
entries.claim: Allowing phones in lessons undermines concentration.
entries.because: Notifications, games and social media tempt pupils to glance at their screens, and even a brief interruption breaks the train of thought needed to follow an explanation.
entries.result: Teachers report smoother lessons and more participation when phones are out of sight.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề cấm điện thoại, mạng xã hội, thiết bị trong lớp.

entries.label_vi: Điện thoại → gian lận, quay lén, bắt nạt mạng; cấm là quy tắc đơn giản, dễ thực thi
entries.claim: Unrestricted phone use exposes students to misuse, from cheating to cyberbullying.
entries.because: Phones make it easy to cheat, record classmates without consent or circulate hurtful messages, and teachers cannot monitor every screen.
entries.result: A clear ban removes these temptations.
entries.rebuttal: Phones are useful and parents need contact, but schools can provide computers, allow phones in designated sessions and route emergencies through the office.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề cấm điện thoại, an toàn mạng, kỷ luật.

entries.text: A child who is passionate about astronomy, for example, can spend extra weeks exploring the subject instead of moving on after a single lesson.
A child taught entirely at home, for instance, may find a first job interview or group project unusually daunting.
A parent with no scientific background, for example, may struggle to guide a teenager through chemistry experiments.
A science teacher required to deliver chemistry in a second language, for example, must first master the specialist vocabulary herself.
A pupil whose results suddenly decline, for example, may be struggling with bullying or problems at home, and an early conversation can address the cause rather than only the symptoms.
A pupil who keeps checking messages during a mathematics explanation, for instance, falls behind and then struggles with the homework.
